blind.second_guess: broken stone floor tile or grave slab
blind.description: A rectangular carved stone architectural slab broken across the center into two pieces, resting atop a flat bed of small stones and rubble. Each half has a beveled perimeter rim and a slightly recessed rectangular central panel with stylized chiseled edges. Surfaces are solid, smooth, and sculpted in a hand-painted/stylized art style. The material is dark weathered grey-brown stone with lighter edge highlights. It sits firmly on the ground via the rubble base with no floating or disconnected parts.
blind.from_above: A vertically-oriented rectangular stone slab broken crosswise through the middle by an irregular crack into two pieces, framed by a recessed inner panel, with small rubble stones visible protruding around the lateral edges.
blind.extra_base_or_ground: bed of rubble and small stones integrated into the base
blind.height_vs_figure: About 1/4 as tall as the 5 ft 9 in figure (roughly 1.3 to 1.5 ft high), about 4 to 5 ft long, and about 3 ft wide.
